subject.title: fix: allow bailian provider in resolveThinkingProfile

question: Should OpenClaw support custom `bailian` Qwen thinking inference by default while keeping Bailian policy out of the vLLM plugin?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent support boundary affects provider/model capability behavior for existing Bailian configs and the broader Coding Plan issue remains open.

options.title: Accept Narrow Custom-Provider Support
options.body: Land only the configured-provider Bailian inference path after proof shows a config where this PR changes behavior, while leaving bundled Coding Plan catalog work on the canonical issue.

options.title: Fold Into Qwen Provider Work
options.body: Pause this PR and require the broader Qwen/Coding Plan provider-owned fix to handle bundled catalog and custom-provider behavior together.

options.title: Keep Current Conservative Behavior
options.body: Do not infer Bailian Qwen thinking until maintainers have model-by-model vendor proof for the affected Coding Plan endpoints.

recommendation.title: Accept Narrow Custom-Provider Support
recommendation.body: Land only the configured-provider Bailian inference path after proof shows a config where this PR changes behavior, while leaving bundled Coding Plan catalog work on the canonical issue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is already tied to the prior issue routing and adjacent Qwen provider support-boundary decisions.
